text:
Taylor Nguyen: Hi team, quick onboarding question. I found a hosted API key in the vault under our team folder. Should I wire that into our CI to run streaming integration tests, or use the sandbox key? I'm worried about 429s/quotas.
Priya Patel: welcome! :wave: Short answer: prefer sandbox for dev/CI unless you need production routing/latency or throughput that sandbox can't handle. Sandbox is shared so quotas are lower and you will hit 429s if you parallelize too much.
Taylor Nguyen: got it. If we do need more throughput for nightly CI, what's the process to get a hosted test quota?
Maya Ortiz: open an ops-support ticket with team name, repo/pipeline id, expected sustained qps and max burst, and the window (e.g., nightly 02:00-06:00 UTC). Ops will provision a temporary hosted quota or add your CI runner IPs to an allowlist. Example body: "team=search-infra repo=search/ci pipeline=nightly qps=12 burst=60 concurrency=30 window=02-06UTC reason=integration + perf smoke"
Taylor Nguyen: is there a ticket template somewhere I can copy?
Maya Ortiz: Yup, use the ops board template or paste this: 
``n
Title: hosted-test-quota-request - search-infra
Body:
- Team: search-infra
- Repo: search/ci
- Pipeline: nightly-integration
- Requested QPS: 12
- Burst: 60
- Expected duration: 2h/night
- CI runner IPs (if allowlist preferred): 3.23.45.67, 3.23.45.68
- Reason: run streaming integration tests validating chunked responses and latency

``n
Ops usually responds same day for test requests.
DevEx Bot: Ephemeral keys are recommended for CI. Command to mint a short-lived token: 
```
./devex auth mint --role=ci-runner --ttl=3h --repo=search/ci --scope=streaming
# writes token to /tmp/devex_token
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat /tmp/devex_token)
```
The token is auto-revoked after ttl. DevEx portal: https://redwood.internal/devex/ephemeral-keys
Taylor Nguyen: nice. One more: our streaming tests split work into many parallel streams and we see 429s in sandbox even with low qps per stream. Is that expected?
Priya Patel: yes, sandbox rate limits are global/shared and streaming counts against concurrency and token throughput. For streaming test flavors: reduce concurrency, use sequential streams in CI, or stub responses for unit-level CI. If you must parallelize for e2e perf, request hosted test quota with concurrency numbers. Also add exponential backoff and jitter on 429s for flakiness.
Ops Support Bot: Security reminder: never commit hosted keys to a repo. Use secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager / GitHub Actions secrets) and ephemeral tokens when possible. If you need a long-lived hosted key for integration, we'll require IP allowlist + IAM role binding + approval ticket.
Taylor Nguyen: great, I'll try ephemeral tokens for now and paste the ops ticket using Maya's template if we need hosted quota. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Maya Ortiz: ping me if you want me to file the ticket on your behalf.
Taylor Nguyen: will do, appreciate it!
